content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Let's create a model of a toy car. For the body, create a box with size 200x100x100 mm. Subtract a block of size 50x100x50 at an edge for the windshield part. Add four cylindrical wheels, each with a radius of 25 mm and a thickness of 10 mm. Place the wheels so that they are exactly aligned with the four bottom corners of the car body. The wheels should be embedded into the body, forming half-cylinders oriented along the Y-Axis (positive and negative). They should point inward and must not protrude beyond the sides of the car body. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Below is the logical construction sequence, strictly in terms of the available functions.  
No code is executed yet – this is only the verbal, step-by-step plan you asked for.

1. Build the main car body with one rectangular block  
   • Call functions.block once with  
     – x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100]  
     – x = [0], y = [0], z = [0] (so the body spans 0-200 in X, 0-100 in Y, 0-100 in Z)  
     – subtraction = [False] because it is the very first solid.

2. Carve out the windshield recess (a rectangular subtraction)  
   • Call functions.block a second time with  
     – x_size = [50], y_size = [100], z_size = [50]  
     – x = [150], y = [0], z = [50]  
       (This removes a 50 mm deep, full-width chunk from the front-top edge: X 150-200, Y 0-100, Z 50-100)  
     – subtraction = [True] so the volume is subtracted.

3. Add the four wheels as half-cylinders that are flush with the long side faces and sit at the four bottom corners.  
   Geometry logic for every wheel: the cylinder axis is parallel to ±Y, its “outer” flat face is exactly on the side of the body, and the axis length (thickness) is 10 mm, all embedded inward so nothing sticks out.

   Wheel A (front-left, pointing +Y inward)  
   • functions.cylinder with  
     – baseCenterX = [25]          (one radius in from the front in X)  
     – baseCenterY = [0]           (outer left side)  
     – baseCenterZ = [25]          (radius above ground)  
     – heightVectX  = [0]  
     – heightVectY  = [10]         (into the body, +Y direction)  
     – heightVectZ  = [0]  
     – radius      = [25]  
     – subtraction = [False]  
     – cylinder_func = [0]

   Wheel B (front-right, pointing −Y inward)  
   • baseCenterX = [25]  
   • baseCenterY = [100]  
   • baseCenterZ = [25]  
   • heightVectY = [-10]           (into the body, −Y)  
   (other parameters identical)

   Wheel C (rear-left, pointing +Y inward)  
   • baseCenterX = [175]           (200 – 25)  
   • baseCenterY = [0]  
   • baseCenterZ = [25]  
   • heightVectY = [10]  
   (other parameters identical)

   Wheel D (rear-right, pointing −Y inward)  
   • baseCenterX = [175]  
   • baseCenterY = [100]  
   • baseCenterZ = [25]  
   • heightVectY = [-10]  
   (other parameters identical)

4. Finalise  
   • Call functions.finished with allFunctionsCalled = true when all above geometry-creating calls have been issued.

If this plan is satisfactory, tell me to “prepare the function calls,” and I will respond with the exact functions.*
